questions.q: A 28-year-old man presents with a painless hypopigmented patch on his left forearm with decreased sensation to light touch. Slit-skin smear is negative. Skin biopsy shows non-caseating granulomas around dermal nerves with lymphocytic infiltrate. Which type of leprosy does this most likely represent?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) presents with a single or few well-defined hypopigmented patches with clear-cut borders, marked sensory loss, and negative slit-skin smear. Biopsy shows well-formed non-caseating granulomas with epithelioid cells and lymphocytes around neurovascular bundles.

questions.q: A 35-year-old leprosy patient on multidrug therapy (MDT) develops sudden onset erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL). Which of the following drugs is the treatment of choice for recurrent, steroid-dependent ENL?
questions.exp: Thalidomide is the treatment of choice for recurrent and steroid-dependent ENL. It inhibits TNF-alpha production. Clofazimine is used for long-term ENL suppression but thalidomide is preferred for acute recurrent cases. It is teratogenic and contraindicated in women of childbearing age.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with a tense blistering eruption predominantly on the flexural areas and lower abdomen. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposits at the dermoepidermal junction. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid (BP) presents with tense blisters on flexural areas, negative Nikolsky sign, and linear IgG/C3 at the BMZ on DIF. The autoantibodies target BP180 (type XVII collagen) and BP230. It is the most common autoimmune blistering disorder in the elderly.

questions.q: A 50-year-old woman presents with flaccid blisters and erosions involving the oral mucosa and scalp for 3 months. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF of perilesional skin shows intercellular IgG deposits in the epidermis in a 'fishnet' pattern. The target antigen is most likely:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris primarily targets desmoglein 3 (Dsg3), which is predominant in the mucous membranes. Mucosal-dominant pemphigus is associated with anti-Dsg3 antibodies alone, whereas mucocutaneous pemphigus has both anti-Dsg3 and anti-Dsg1 antibodies.

questions.q: A 22-year-old athlete presents with scaling and erythema in the groin area sparing the scrotum. KOH preparation shows septate hyphae. The most likely causative organism is:
questions.exp: Tinea cruris (jock itch) classically spares the scrotum, differentiating it from candidal intertrigo which involves the scrotum. Epidermophyton floccosum is a common cause of tinea cruris and does not infect hair. Trichophyton rubrum is also common but E. floccosum is the classic teaching point for scrotal sparing.

questions.q: A 25-year-old man presents with asymptomatic hypopigmented and hyperpigmented macules on the trunk. Under Wood's lamp, the lesions show golden-yellow fluorescence. KOH shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' pattern. What is the treatment of choice?
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor is caused by Malassezia furfur (now M. globosa). The characteristic KOH finding is 'spaghetti and meatballs' (short hyphae and spores). First-line treatment is topical antifungals like selenium sulfide or ketoconazole. Oral itraconazole is used for extensive or recurrent cases.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman with photosensitivity presents with a malar rash, oral ulcers, and arthritis. ANA is positive with anti-dsDNA antibodies. Skin biopsy of both involved and uninvolved sun-exposed skin shows immunoglobulin deposits at the dermoepidermal junction. This finding is called:
questions.exp: The lupus band test (LBT) refers to the finding of immunoglobulin (IgG, IgM, IgA) and complement deposits at the dermoepidermal junction on DIF. In SLE, the LBT is positive in both lesional AND non-lesional sun-exposed skin, unlike DLE where it is positive only in lesional skin.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with proximal muscle weakness, heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules over the knuckles, and periungual telangiectasias. Which malignancy is most commonly associated with this condition in adult female patients?
questions.exp: Dermatomyositis in adults carries a significant risk of underlying malignancy (~15-25%). In women, ovarian carcinoma is the most commonly associated malignancy. In men, gastric and nasopharyngeal carcinomas are more common. Lung and breast cancers are also associated but ovarian is the classic teaching point for female DM.

questions.q: A 14-year-old boy presents with honey-colored crusted lesions around the nose and mouth after an upper respiratory tract infection. The lesions began as vesicles that rapidly ruptured. The most likely causative organism is:
opts: Both Staphylococcus aureus and Streptococcus pyogenes
questions.exp: Impetigo contagiosa is most commonly caused by Staphylococcus aureus, Streptococcus pyogenes, or both. The classic non-bullous impetigo with honey-colored crusts is frequently caused by S. pyogenes alone or mixed infection. Bullous impetigo is caused exclusively by S. aureus (phage type 71) producing exfoliative toxins.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child develops widespread erythema, skin tenderness, and superficial exfoliation giving a 'scalded skin' appearance. There is no mucous membrane involvement. Nikolsky sign is positive. The causative staphylococcal toxin acts by cleaving:
questions.exp: Staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome (SSSS) is caused by exfoliative toxins A and B produced by S. aureus phage group II. These toxins are serine proteases that specifically cleave desmoglein 1 in the superficial epidermis, causing subcorneal blistering. Mucous membranes are spared as Dsg1 is absent there.

questions.q: A 28-year-old sexually active man presents with a painless indurated ulcer on the glans penis with clean edges and a serous exudate. Inguinal lymph nodes are enlarged, firm, and non-tender. Dark-field microscopy would likely demonstrate:
questions.exp: The painless, indurated ulcer with non-tender lymphadenopathy is classic for primary syphilis (chancre). Dark-field microscopy of the serous exudate demonstrates Treponema pallidum with characteristic corkscrew morphology and motility. This is the most sensitive direct method for diagnosing primary syphilis.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with multiple painful genital ulcers with undermined, ragged edges and soft consistency. There is tender inguinal lymphadenopathy with fluctuant nodes (buboes). Gram stain shows 'school of fish' appearance of gram-negative rods. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Chancroid (soft chancre) caused by Haemophilus ducreyi presents with painful soft ulcers with undermined edges. Gram stain shows gram-negative coccobacilli in 'school of fish' or 'railroad track' pattern. Painful suppurative buboes are characteristic. Treatment is azithromycin 1g single dose or ceftriaxone 250mg IM.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a pearly, translucent papule with rolled borders and telangiectasias on the nose. The lesion has been slowly growing over 2 years. The most common histological subtype of this tumour is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma (BCC) is the most common skin cancer. The nodular subtype is the most common, presenting as a pearly, translucent papule or nodule with rolled borders and telangiectasias, most often on the nose and central face. The morpheaform subtype is the most aggressive and most likely to recur.

questions.q: A 60-year-old chronic sun-exposed farmer presents with a rapidly growing keratotic nodule on the lower lip. Biopsy confirms well-differentiated invasive squamous cell carcinoma. Which histological feature is the strongest predictor of poor prognosis?
questions.exp: Perineural invasion is the most important poor prognostic factor for cutaneous SCC, associated with higher rates of local recurrence, regional metastasis, and disease-specific mortality. Other poor prognostic features include depth >2mm, poor differentiation, immunosuppression, and location on the lip or ear.

questions.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scales on the elbows, knees, and scalp. She has associated nail pitting and onycholysis. Which drug is most likely to exacerbate her condition?
questions.exp: Lithium is a well-known trigger and exacerbator of psoriasis. Other drugs that worsen psoriasis include beta-blockers, antimalarials (chloroquine), NSAIDs, ACE inhibitors, and systemic corticosteroid withdrawal. Lithium acts by inhibiting inositol monophosphatase and affects keratinocyte proliferation.

questions.q: A 20-year-old woman presents with comedones, inflammatory papules, and nodules on the face and back that have not responded adequately to 6 months of topical benzoyl peroxide and topical antibiotics. Which oral medication is indicated for severe nodulocystic acne?
questions.exp: Oral isotretinoin (13-cis-retinoic acid) is indicated for severe nodulocystic/conglobate acne or acne unresponsive to conventional therapy. It is the only treatment that targets all four pathogenic factors: sebum production, follicular hyperkeratinization, P. acnes colonization, and inflammation. Mandatory pregnancy prevention is required due to teratogenicity.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman presents with persistent facial flushing, erythema, and papulopustules over the central face without comedones. She reports worsening with hot beverages and sun exposure. The first-line topical treatment for the papulopustular component is:
questions.exp: Rosacea (papulopustular subtype) is characterized by facial erythema with papulopustules but without comedones (distinguishing it from acne). First-line topical agents include metronidazole 0.75-1% gel/cream and azelaic acid 15% gel. Topical ivermectin 1% cream targeting Demodex is also effective. Tretinoin is for acne, not rosacea.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman of skin type IV presents with bilateral symmetrical brown patches on the cheeks and upper lip that darken in summer. Wood's lamp examination enhances the pigmentation. The most effective topical treatment combination is:
opts: Triple combination cream (hydroquinone 4% + tretinoin 0.05% + fluocinolone acetonide 0.01%)
questions.exp: Melasma treatment requires a multimodal approach. The triple combination cream (modified Kligman's formula: hydroquinone + retinoid + mild corticosteroid) is the most effective first-line topical treatment. Hydroquinone inhibits tyrosinase, tretinoin increases epidermal turnover, and the corticosteroid reduces irritation. Strict photoprotection is mandatory.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with depigmented macules on the dorsum of hands and around the mouth. His thyroid function tests reveal hypothyroidism. Which autoimmune condition is most commonly associated with vitiligo?
questions.exp: Autoimmune thyroid diseases (Hashimoto's thyroiditis and Graves' disease) are the most common autoimmune associations with vitiligo, occurring in 15-30% of patients. Routine thyroid function testing is recommended in all vitiligo patients. Other associations include Type 1 DM, Addison's disease, and pernicious anemia.

questions.q: A 28-year-old man on dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis develops pallor, jaundice, and haemoglobin drops to 7g/dL. Blood smear shows Heinz bodies. He is most likely deficient in:
questions.exp: Dapsone can cause dose-dependent hemolytic anemia and methemoglobinemia in all patients, but these are severe in G6PD-deficient patients. G6PD deficiency impairs the cell's ability to neutralize oxidative stress from dapsone metabolites, leading to Heinz body hemolytic anemia. G6PD screening before initiating dapsone is recommended.

questions.q: A 42-year-old woman on carbamazepine for trigeminal neuralgia develops high fever, widespread confluent erythema, and epidermal detachment involving >30% BSA with severe mucosal erosions. The epidermal detachment in this condition is at which histological level?
opts: Full-thickness epidermal necrosis at the DEJ
questions.exp: Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN) involves full-thickness epidermal necrosis and detachment at the dermo-epidermal junction. The mechanism involves keratinocyte apoptosis mediated by cytotoxic T lymphocytes and granulysin. Mucosal involvement distinguishes it from SSSS (which is subcorneal/superficial). Mortality can reach 30-40%.

questions.q: A 19-year-old man presents with grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the right forehead and tip of nose with intense pain. The involvement of the tip of nose in herpes zoster is significant because it predicts:
questions.exp: Hutchinson's sign — vesicles at the tip and side of the nose — indicates involvement of the nasociliary branch of V1, which also innervates the globe. This sign predicts a 76% risk of ocular complications (keratitis, uveitis, scleritis). Urgent ophthalmology referral is mandatory. Ramsay Hunt syndrome involves the geniculate ganglion causing facial palsy and ear vesicles.

questions.q: A 35-year-old immunocompetent woman presents with a painless 3mm umbilicated pearly papule on the inner thigh. Similar lesions are on her 6-year-old child's face. Histology of the papule's core would show:
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum is caused by a poxvirus. Histology shows large intracytoplasmic inclusion bodies (Henderson-Patterson bodies or molluscum bodies) that displace the nucleus to the periphery. Cowdry type A inclusions are seen in herpesvirus infections. Guarnieri bodies are in smallpox/vaccinia. Negri bodies are in rabies.

questions.q: A 26-year-old woman presents with pruritic papules and burrows in the interdigital web spaces, wrists, and areolae. Her partner has similar symptoms. Dermoscopy reveals a 'jet with contrail' sign. The recommended treatment is:
questions.exp: Topical permethrin 5% cream is the first-line treatment for scabies, applied from neck to toe and washed off after 8-14 hours, repeated after 1 week. Oral ivermectin is used for crusted (Norwegian) scabies or when topical therapy fails. All household and close contacts should be treated simultaneously to prevent reinfestation.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man with chronic plaque psoriasis involving 30% BSA fails multiple systemic therapies. He is started on a biologic specifically targeting IL-17A. Which agent is this?
questions.exp: Secukinumab (Cosentyx) is a fully human monoclonal antibody that specifically targets IL-17A. Other IL-17 pathway inhibitors include ixekizumab (anti-IL-17A) and bimekizumab (anti-IL-17A and F). Ustekinumab targets IL-12/23 (p40 subunit). Guselkumab targets IL-23 (p19 subunit). Adalimumab targets TNF-alpha.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with a verrucous plaque on the right leg slowly enlarging over 15 years. He is a farmer. Biopsy shows pseudoepitheliomatous hyperplasia and thick-walled, dark-brown fungal cells dividing in multiple planes (Medlar/sclerotic bodies). The most common causative organism worldwide is:
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is a chronic deep fungal infection caused by dematiaceous (black) fungi. Fonsecaea pedrosoi is the most common causative organism worldwide. Medlar bodies (sclerotic cells/copper pennies) are the diagnostic hallmark: brown, thick-walled cells with septation in multiple planes. Treatment is oral itraconazole, often combined with cryotherapy.

questions.q: A 30-year-old man with HIV (CD4 count 45 cells/mm3) develops painless violaceous papules and plaques on the hard palate and legs. Biopsy shows spindle cells with slit-like vascular spaces and extravasated red blood cells. HHV-8 serology is positive. First-line systemic treatment for disseminated disease is:
questions.exp: Kaposi's sarcoma in advanced HIV (epidemic KS) associated with HHV-8 requires systemic therapy when disseminated. Liposomal doxorubicin (pegylated, e.g., Doxil) is the first-line systemic chemotherapy. Antiretroviral therapy (ART) should also be initiated/optimized. Localized lesions can be treated with radiation, cryotherapy, or intralesional agents.

questions.q: A 55-year-old woman presents with superficial scaly patches and plaques on the lower trunk and buttocks for 10 years. Biopsy shows epidermotropism of atypical lymphocytes with Pautrier's microabscesses. IHC is CD3+, CD4+, CD8-. The next step in staging is:
opts: Peripheral blood flow cytometry for CD4:CD8 ratio and Sezary cell count
T-cell receptor gene rearrangement study on blood
questions.exp: Mycosis fungoides (MF) is the most common primary cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. After skin biopsy confirms MF, staging includes peripheral blood evaluation for Sezary cells by flow cytometry (CD4:CD8 ratio >10, or Sezary cells >1000/mm3 indicates blood involvement, stage B2). Early-stage MF is treated with skin-directed therapies.

questions.q: During Mohs micrographic surgery (MMS), what unique advantage does this technique have over conventional excision with standard margins?
opts: It does not require local anesthesia
It allows examination of 100% of the surgical margin using horizontal frozen sections
It stimulates faster wound healing by secondary intention
It eliminates the need for histopathological assessment
questions.exp: Mohs micrographic surgery allows real-time histologic examination of 100% of the peripheral and deep surgical margin using horizontal (en face) frozen sections, unlike conventional excision which samples <1% of margins using vertical bread-loaf sections. This allows precise tumor mapping, maximal tissue conservation, and the lowest reported recurrence rates for high-risk tumours.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman with severe atopic dermatitis fails topical corticosteroids and topical calcineurin inhibitors. She is started on dupilumab. What is dupilumab's mechanism of action?
opts: Blocks IL-4Rα subunit, thereby inhibiting both IL-4 and IL-13 signaling
Blocks IL-31 receptor to reduce itch
questions.exp: Dupilumab is a fully human monoclonal antibody targeting the IL-4 receptor alpha (IL-4Rα) subunit, which is shared by the type I receptor (IL-4Rα/γc) and type II receptor (IL-4Rα/IL-13Rα1). Blocking IL-4Rα simultaneously inhibits both IL-4 and IL-13 signaling — the key Th2 cytokines driving atopic dermatitis. JAK inhibitors (abrocitinib, upadacitinib) are also approved for moderate-severe AD.

questions.q: A 40-year-old man presents with pruritic grouped vesicles on extensor surfaces of elbows and knees, and buttocks. Skin biopsy shows subepidermal blisters with neutrophil microabscesses at the dermal papillae tips. DIF shows granular IgA deposits in dermal papillae. This condition is most strongly associated with:
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis (DH) is the cutaneous manifestation of coeliac disease (gluten-sensitive enteropathy). Virtually all DH patients have subclinical or clinical coeliac disease. Granular IgA deposits in the dermal papillae on DIF is pathognomonic. Treatment is a strict gluten-free diet and dapsone for symptomatic relief.
